The Brief in this order is a different object; never index _protocol with Brief keys. Continuous measurements are never identifiers, however many distinct values they have. Exclude, in the saved preprocessing, only features that are confirmed derivations of a target: exact equality with it, or a row sum of up to three non-negative columns that equals it on every training row. Features with absolute correlation of 0.98 or more with a target are a warning, not proof: keep them and print one line with their names. Print one line naming any excluded feature and the reason. Correlation warnings apply only to numeric outcomes; never coerce categorical labels to floats for Pearson correlation. Skip that numeric screen for categorical outcomes and retain exact-derivation checks.
[RL-0009] Keep feature names through preprocessing. When the encoded output has at most 300 columns, call set_output(transform='pandas') on ColumnTransformer and Pipeline objects and use OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False). When it would be wider, keep sparse output inside one Pipeline that starts from the raw feature DataFrame, take names from get_feature_names_out(), and never pass that output to a transformer that selects columns by name. Use set_output only with components that support it; prefer built-in sklearn transformers with get_feature_names_out rather than custom components.
[RL-0010] Before encoding, sort feature columns into types: numeric; low-cardinality categorical (one-hot); text or code columns with more unique values than 5% of rows (drop, or use a frequency encoding fitted on training rows, never one-hot); date or time strings (parse with pandas.to_datetime, derive numeric parts such as hour, day of week and month, then drop the raw string). Columns already of datetime type get the same treatment: numeric parts or days elapsed since a fixed reference date, then drop the raw column; never pass a datetime column to an imputer, scaler, encoder or model. This includes date columns created in earlier steps, such as first and last dates in entity aggregates: check dtypes of the frame you fit on, not only of the raw table. Integer 0/1 indicator columns stay numeric.
[RL-0012] Summary tables have one type per column: use NaN, not empty strings, for values that do not apply, or put numeric and categorical summaries in separate columns. Keep at most 50 rows and 12 columns; for wide summaries, place variables in rows and statistics in columns.
[RL-0013] Keep each script short and direct, about 120 lines or fewer: loop over columns instead of repeating blocks, no commented-out alternatives, no long docstrings, no restating of these instructions. A complete short script is better than an elaborate one that is cut off.
[RL-0014] When repairing, read the error type and message in the diagnostics first and change the smallest part of the script that causes it; keep the approach, inputs and outputs. A message about specifying columns with strings on non-dataframes means an array reached a name-based transformer (see RL-0009 and RL-0011). A KeyError on a JSON key means a guessed structure; use the keys the file has. Messages starting with 'MLCA:' state an engine rule; comply, do not work around it.
[RL-0015] When the training table has more than 100000 rows, avoid methods whose cost grows with the square of the row count (full silhouette, kernel SVMs, pairwise distances, t-SNE, agglomerative clustering) and prefer linear models with saga or SGD solvers, HistGradientBoosting or MiniBatchKMeans. Every fit_record call still uses all training rows; compute expensive diagnostics that fit nothing on a fixed-seed subsample of at most 10000 rows and print its size.
[RL-0023] Check text columns for placeholder tokens that stand for missing values (a lone '?', '-', 'NA', 'N/A', or whitespace-only strings) and for surrounding whitespace. Strip whitespace and convert only such placeholders to missing inside the fitted preprocessing, and print one line naming the placeholders found and how many columns contain them.
[RL-0025] Save objects that can load in a fresh Python interpreter using installed packages alone. Prefer built-in sklearn estimators, selectors and transformers. Never pickle locally defined estimators, functions or lambdas: they depend on an earlier script's __main__ and cannot be loaded reliably later. For an identity selector use an importable built-in passthrough transformer, not a custom wrapper. Switching to joblib does not restore missing definitions. Never fabricate replacement behavior to make an incompatible saved object load.
[RL-0026] Persist the full row-preserving feature transformation contract, not just an estimator fitted after transient DataFrame mutations. Parsing, derived features, column selection and ordering needed later must be reproducible by the saved importable pipeline. Learned transforms fit only on the frozen training rows. Deterministic table preparation may precede the split only through a declared prepared-data artifact. Later steps pass the declared source feature schema to the saved pipeline, never assume derived columns already exist in a freshly loaded partition. Inspect fitted input names; do not invent missing columns or fit replacement preprocessing during evaluation.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder

mlca_runtime.set_seed(42)
inp = mlca_runtime.inputs()
proto = json.loads(inp['_protocol'].read_text())
for k in ('targets', 'excluded_columns', 'task'):
    if k not in proto:
        raise ValueError(f"missing {k}; available: {list(proto.keys())}")
targets = proto['targets']; excluded = proto['excluded_columns']
group = proto.get('group_column')
train = pd.read_parquet(inp['train']); val = pd.read_parquet(inp['val'])

blocked = set(targets) | set(excluded) | ({group} if group else set())
feats = [c for c in train.columns if c not in blocked]

def is_keylike(s):
    if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s) and s.dtype.kind in 'iu':
        return s.notna().all() and s.nunique() == len(s)
    if s.dtype == object or isinstance(s.dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype):
        return s.notna().all() and s.nunique() == len(s)
    return False

keys = [c for c in feats if is_keylike(train[c])]
feats = [c for c in feats if c not in keys]

tgt = train[targets[0]] if targets[0] in train else None
derived = [c for c in feats if tgt is not None and train[c].equals(tgt)]
for c in derived:
    print(f"excluded {c}: exact derivation of target")
feats = [c for c in feats if c not in derived]

n = len(train)
num_cols, cat_cols, date_cols, drop_cols = [], [], [], []
for c in feats:
    s = train[c]
    if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(s):
        date_cols.append(c)
    elif pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s) and not pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s):
        num_cols.append(c)
    elif s.dtype == object or isinstance(s.dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype) or pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(s):
        if s.nunique(dropna=True) > 0.05 * n:
            drop_cols.append(c)
        else:
            cat_cols.append(c)
    else:
        num_cols.append(c)

for d in date_cols:
    dt = pd.to_datetime(train[d], errors='coerce'); dv = pd.to_datetime(val[d], errors='coerce')
    for part, fn_t, fn_v in [('year', dt.dt.year, dv.dt.year),
                             ('month', dt.dt.month, dv.dt.month),
                             ('dayofweek', dt.dt.dayofweek, dv.dt.dayofweek)]:
        name = f"{d}_{part}"
        train[name] = fn_t; val[name] = fn_v
        num_cols.append(name)

ph_cols = []
for c in cat_cols:
    s = train[c].astype('string').str.strip()
    if s.isin(['?', '-', 'NA', 'N/A']).any() or s.eq('').any():
        ph_cols.append(c)
print(f"feats={len(feats)} num={len(num_cols)} cat={len(cat_cols)} drops={len(drop_cols)} key={len(keys)} ph={len(ph_cols)}")

pre = ColumnTransformer(
    [('num', Pipeline([('imp', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')),
                       ('sc', StandardScaler())]), num_cols),
     ('cat', Pipeline([('imp', SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent')),
                       ('oh', OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False))]), cat_cols)],
    remainder='drop')
pre.set_output(transform='pandas')

Xtr = train[num_cols + cat_cols].copy()
Xva = val.reindex(columns=Xtr.columns).copy()
y = train[targets[0]] if targets[0] in train else None
fitted = mlca_runtime.fit_record(pre, Xtr, 'train', y=y)
Xt = fitted.transform(Xva)
print(f"train {Xtr.shape} val {Xva.shape} -> transformed {Xt.shape}")
mlca_runtime.save_model(fitted, 'preprocessor')

import json
import mlca_runtime
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder

mlca_runtime.set_seed(42)
inp = mlca_runtime.inputs()
proto = json.loads(inp['_protocol'].read_text())
for k in ('targets', 'excluded_columns', 'task'):
    if k not in proto:
        raise ValueError(f"missing key {k}; available top-level keys: {sorted(proto.keys())}")
targets = list(proto['targets'])
excluded = list(proto['excluded_columns'])
group = proto.get('group_column')
train = pd.read_parquet(inp['train'])
val = pd.read_parquet(inp['val'])

blocked = set(targets) | set(excluded) | ({group} if group else set())
cand = [c for c in train.columns if c not in blocked]


def keylike(s):
    if s.isna().any():
        return False
    if pd.api.types.is_integer_dtype(s) and not pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s):
        return s.nunique() == len(s)
    if pd.api.types.is_object_dtype(s) or isinstance(s.dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype):
        return s.nunique() == len(s)
    return False


keys = [c for c in cand if keylike(train[c])]
feats = [c for c in cand if c not in keys]

target = targets[0]
derived = [c for c in feats if train[c].equals(train[target])]
for c in derived:
    print(f"excluded {c}: exact derivation of target {target}")
feats = [c for c in feats if c not in derived]

n = len(train)
num_cols, cat_cols, date_cols, drop_cols = [], [], [], []
for c in feats:
    s = train[c]
    if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(s):
        date_cols.append(c)
    elif pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s) and not pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s):
        num_cols.append(c)
    elif pd.api.types.is_object_dtype(s) or isinstance(s.dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype) or pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(s):
        if s.nunique(dropna=True) > 0.05 * n:
            drop_cols.append(c)
        else:
            cat_cols.append(c)
    else:
        num_cols.append(c)

for d in date_cols:
    dt = pd.to_datetime(train[d], errors='coerce')
    dv = pd.to_datetime(val[d], errors='coerce')
    for part in ('year', 'month', 'dayofweek'):
        name = f"{d}_{part}"
        train[name] = getattr(dt.dt, part)
        val[name] = getattr(dv.dt, part)
        num_cols.append(name)

tokens = ['?', '-', 'NA', 'N/A']
ph_cols = [c for c in cat_cols
           if train[c].astype('string').str.strip().isin(tokens + ['']).any()]
print(f"feats={len(feats)} num={len(num_cols)} cat={len(cat_cols)} "
      f"dropped={len(drop_cols)} keys={len(keys)} placeholder_cols={len(ph_cols)}")

width = len(num_cols) + sum(int(train[c].nunique(dropna=True)) + 1 for c in cat_cols)
parts = [('num', Pipeline([('imp', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')),
                           ('sc', StandardScaler())]), num_cols),
         ('cat', Pipeline([('imp', SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent')),
                           ('oh', OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False))]), cat_cols)]
parts = [p for p in parts if p[2]]
pre = ColumnTransformer(parts, remainder='drop', verbose_feature_names_out=False)
if width <= 300:
    pre.set_output(transform='pandas')

cols = num_cols + cat_cols
Xtr = train[cols]
Xva = val.reindex(columns=cols)
fitted = mlca_runtime.fit_record(pre, Xtr, 'train', y=train[target])
Xt = fitted.transform(Xva)
names = fitted.get_feature_names_out() if width <= 300 else None
print(f"train {Xtr.shape} val {Xva.shape} -> encoded {Xt.shape}")
mlca_runtime.save_model(fitted, 'preprocessor.pkl')
